🇲🇽🏫 <u>Mexico City Goes for a 6x Expansion of Early Childhood Education</u>

Only 13% of Mexico City's 273,000 children aged 0-3 have access to early education. Clara Brugada's government plans to go from 217 to 617 centers and from 12,000 to 72,000 kids by 2030, backed by a constitutional reform that makes early education public, free and mandatory for future administrations to fund. "In this city, education starts in the cradle," Brugada said. It also frees mothers to go back to work.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>US and Chinese Embassies Brawl Over Fentanyl — Mexico in the Middle</u>

While Sheinbaum was in Shenzhen at APEC, Ambassador Ronald Johnson's US Embassy in Mexico posted that "fentanyl doesn't start in Mexico" but in China. Beijing's embassy fired back: "The fentanyl crisis in that country was caused neither by China nor by Mexico," blaming US regulatory failures and drug abuse, and noted that China and Mexico already run a joint working group on chemical precursors. It told Washington's diplomats to spend their time on "pragmatic cooperation" with Mexico instead of slander.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Maize Growers Win: 950 Pesos More Per Ton, Blockades Lifted</u>

After highway blockades across Guanajuato, Jalisco and Michoacán, Mexico's Agriculture Ministry (Sader) put a federal incentive of 950 pesos per ton of white maize on the table, lifting the guaranteed price from 5,226 to 6,176 pesos for the spring-summer 2026 harvest in six states. Growers selling to livestock buyers get another 300 pesos per ton for freight. Producers accepted and reopened the roads; talks on 12 remaining demands continue in Mexico City.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Stops Christie's: Frida Kahlo Painting Pulled From Auction</u>

Christie's yanked Frida Kahlo's "Congreso de los pueblos por la paz" — estimated at up to $3.5 million — from its November 17 sale after Mexico's INBAL invoked federal monuments law and demanded proof of provenance and ownership. INBAL says the work is "part of an ongoing investigation by the competent Mexican authorities." Activists say there is no paper trail showing how it left the Frida Kahlo Museum. Mexico's heritage isn't stock for a New York gavel.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico's Dependence on US Diesel Fell From 71% to 45%</u>

In 2018, US imports covered 71% of Mexico's diesel demand. Today they cover 45%, according to BBVA México, cited by El Financiero. Domestic diesel refining doubled from 135,000 barrels a day in 2023 to 273,000 in 2026, and Dos Bocas now handles about a third of all crude refined in the country. The weak spot is storage: Mexico still buys around 220,000 barrels a day from the US, and inventories would cover only 15 to 21 days if that supply were cut off.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE Auditors Find 43 Million Pesos in Irregularities Across Four State Offices</u>

INE's internal comptroller found about 43 million pesos in irregularities at its offices in Nuevo León, Tabasco, Guerrero and Tlaxcala. Nuevo León alone has 34,152,983 pesos still unaccounted for, including caps for staff that were bought but never shown to have been delivered. The comptroller has already told Congress about 16 open investigations, 11 of them into procurement. This is the institute that said cutting its budget would endanger democracy.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE Clean-Up: Five Interim Directors Named After Taddei and 30 Officials Leave</u>

Guadalupe Taddei resigned and 30 members of her team left with her. INE has now installed five interim heads, including at the Federal Voter Registry and the Professional Electoral Service, and says it will keep reviewing posts across its Executive Board. The review covers a corruption scheme, conflicts of interest and administrative irregularities going back through the Taddei, Córdova, Valdés and Ugalde years.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Maize Growers Block 25 Highways, Government Answers With Dialogue and 26 Billion Pesos Paid Directly</u>

Corn producers blocked at least 25 highway points across Guanajuato, Jalisco, Michoacán, Querétaro and Campeche, demanding a fair price per ton of white maize. Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez said negotiating tables at Segob and Sader stay open, and that 26 billion pesos in direct support reach growers "without intermediaries." The money goes to the people who farm, not to the organizations that claim to speak for them.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SpaceX Starship Debris Washes Up on Tamaulipas Beach, Profepa Holds Musk's Company Responsible</u>

Wreckage from the Starship that exploded on the Texas side of the border is now landing on Mexican sand. Profepa inspectors are at Playa Bagdad, Matamoros, and Mexico will require SpaceX to take charge of the waste. Conibio Global has already collected more than 1,500 pieces of booster lining on a nesting beach for endangered sea turtles. Profepa has had a complaint open against SpaceX since November 2025.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Salinas Pliego Threatens to Replace 15,000 Workers With Machines Over the 40-Hour Week</u>

Mexico's billionaire tax-dodger has a message for workers about the 40-hour week reform and minimum wage hikes: machines work 24/7, with no sick leave and no breastfeeding breaks. "I had fifteen thousand cashiers, I'm going to have zero," Ricardo Salinas Pliego said of Banco Azteca. This is the same man who spent years fighting the SAT in court over billions in back taxes.
